## Report

**Task:** Django ticket — make built-in validators include the provided value in `ValidationError` so custom messages can use `%(value)s` (e.g. `"blah" is not a valid email.`).

**Cause:** All built-in validators raised `ValidationError(self.message, code=self.code)` without `params`, so a `%(value)s` placeholder in a custom message had nothing to interpolate. Only `BaseValidator` (Max/Min/Length validators) already passed `params` including `'value'`.

**Fix** — `django/core/validators.py` only (51 insertions, 18 deletions), left uncommitted in the working tree, no test changes:
- `RegexValidator.__call__`, `URLValidator.__call__` (all 5 raise sites), `EmailValidator.__call__` (3 sites), `ProhibitNullCharactersValidator.__call__`: added `params={'value': value}`
- `validate_ipv4_address`, `validate_ipv6_address`, `validate_ipv46_address`: added `params={'value': value}`
- `DecimalValidator`: added `'value': value` to all four `params` dicts (and an explicit `code='invalid'` on the NaN/Infinity branch)
- `FileExtensionValidator`: added `'value': value` to its params

- `tests/runtests.py validators`: 19 tests, `FAILED (failures=2, errors=1, skipped=5)` — the 2 failures + 1 error are **pre-existing**: I reproduced the identical result on the clean tree via `git stash` (HEAD `f4e93919e4`; they're Python 3.12 vs old-Django-3.2-dev incompatibilities in URLValidator newline/IPv6 handling, unrelated to this change).
